known.title: A draft pull request can reach Ready while still behind a required base
A failed mergeability lookup can let green checks reach Ready
Not done: bring main in when a pull request becomes BEHIND during close
The unrelated spotted-record rewrite is outside ONCLASH scope

findings.body:
Gain 3, Work 2, Harm 3
Raise: Functional. The only merge-state refresh after the check wait is guarded by `pr.get("isDraft")`. For an already ready pull request, main can advance during review or CI; GitHub can then report `BEHIND` while `mergeable` remains `MERGEABLE`, because those fields describe different conditions. The wait reads only `mergeable`, so close writes a Ready receipt for a head that a strict up-to-date rule will refuse to merge. The new tests provide `BEHIND` before close's first PR lookup or immediately after making a draft ready, missing this normal interval. GitHub documents the two fields separately: [pull request states](https://docs.github.com/en/graphql/reference/pulls).
findings.title: Not done: bring main in when a pull request becomes BEHIND during close

findings.body:
Gain 4, Work 1, Harm 3
Raise: Gate. This branch moves more than a thousand existing spotted records, including unrelated PRODUCT.md findings, in `plans/spotted.json`. That file is outside ONCLASH's Scope, and Done-when items 1–3 require no change to its records. The large shared-file rewrite creates avoidable conflicts with concurrent changes that record spotted problems—the clash this story is meant to remove.
